title: Sonny and the Distant Music | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka hears something that might be music drifting through the bush — something low and soft and far away that she can never quite find but doesn't want to lose. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
There was something on the wind.

Sunny stood still and listened.

It was music. Or maybe it was the wind itself doing something musical with the reeds by the creek, or a distant creature's call stretched by the night air into something melodic. She wasn't sure. That was part of what made it beautiful.

She walked toward it.

But the more she walked, the more it stayed exactly the same distance away. Close enough to hear. Too far to find. Every time she moved it shifted slightly, as if it were staying just ahead of her.

She stopped walking.

Maybe the music wasn't something to be found.

Maybe it was something to be listened to.

She sat down in the middle of the path and tilted her head and listened properly — not trying to locate it, just trying to receive it. Low notes. Something that rose and fell. A pattern that almost repeated, then changed.

The music — if it was music — went on.

She thought: some beautiful things aren't meant to be understood, only heard.

The sound moved through her and kept going, out past the trees, into the dark, into somewhere she couldn't follow.

She lay down in the soft grass.

The distant music played on.

And it was the sweetest lullaby she had ever not quite heard.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, distant music. Goodnight, little one.
